assumptions: Capture reagents and orthogonal analytics are compatible with study buffers or spike-in controls will be used to control recovery.
Material yield under staged low-shear conditions will be qualitatively sufficient for downstream fractionation and testing at pilot GMP-like scale.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program-specific concerns indicate processing-induced membrane damage can abolish membrane-protected EV signatures while leaving bulk particle counts similar. A staged, lower-shear concentration approach reduces per-cassette cumulative shear and transient high-transmembrane-pressure exposures that plausibly damage EV membranes or mask surface epitopes, thereby preserving membrane integrity and intact-EV-associated cargo protection during scale-relevant concentration.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Orthogonal intact-EV analytic panel post-concentration (capture co-localization with particle peak; detergent/protease sensitivity; protein:particle ratio).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Concentration/process step is hypothesized to be the scale-sensitive control that determines preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV identity signature required by MISEV2023 and program CMC needs; testing this will define a qualitative process gate for identity.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: if assay controls fail or upstream variability dominates, attribute's role as scale-control may be limited.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed signature loss could be assay variability or capture-reagent incompatibility rather than true TFF-induced damage; spike-in or buffer-compatibility controls are required.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed TFF parameter study with orthogonal intact-EV analytics and explicit capture-reagent compatibility controls (including spike-in recovery).
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV identifies processing sensitivity but does not quantify specific TFF parameter causality; program-level prior hypotheses flagged TFF envelope as a candidate driver of signature loss.

edges.competing_explanation: Preserving orthogonal analytic signatures at scale may not suffice to enable in vivo detectability due to administration route or species-specific clearance differences; additional bridging studies will be required.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recoverability tests using materials that pass/fail the TFF envelope identity criteria.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal delivery uncertainty increases operational need for a reproducible drug-substance identity, but cross-species delivery barriers may still prevent downstream in vivo detectability even if identity is preserved.

nodes.statement: High-flux / high-TMP TFF concentration conditions encountered during scale-up can cause shear- or pressure-induced alteration of EV membranes (loss of membrane integrity or epitope masking) without proportionate changes in bulk particle counts.

A staged low-shear concentration envelope (lower TMP/flux per cassette + inline gentle depth prefilter + cassette rotation) reduces the incidence of membrane alteration and preserves intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) compared with the standard high-flux TFF envelope.

Preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV signature after concentration enables use of that signature as an operational manufacturing gate for drug-substance definition and supports downstream potency and comparability assay development.

competing_explanations: Assay interference or capture-reagent incompatibility (not true damage) explains observed signature loss.
Upstream source-cell variability or fractionation differences (not TFF) are the dominant drivers of signature loss.
dependencies: Analytical validation (capture compatibility and spike-in control qualification) prior to comparative TFF runs
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield from >=3 matched lots
Access to controlled TFF hardware and depth-filter consumables
design_question: At scale-relevant concentration steps, does replacing a single high-flux TFF cassette run with a staged low-shear TFF envelope (reduced TMP/flux per cassette + interim gentle depth-filtration step and cassette rotation) preserve an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) while maintaining manufacturable recovery compared with the current high-flux TFF envelope?
expected_measurable_effect: Compared with the current high-flux TFF envelope, the staged low-shear TFF envelope will show preserved co-localization of capture-positive signal with particle-count peaks in density/size fractions, captured signal loss after detergent + protease/RNase (indicating membrane-protection), and qualitatively comparable recovered particle/mass yield sufficient for preliminary GMP-like batch considerations across independent lots.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow applied to post-concentration outputs and fraction-level measurements: (1) fractionation (density-gradient or SEC) with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture on intact fractions; (3) protease/RNase protection assays with and without detergent on captured material; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) spike-in tracer readout per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched paired runs from each conditioned-medium lot: (A) staged low-shear envelope: low TMP/flux per cassette + cassette rotation schedule + inline depth prefilter, run to scale-proxy processed volume; (B) current high-flux TFF envelope (program comparator) run to equivalent cumulative processed volume. Both arms receive identical downstream fractionation and orthogonal analytics and identical spike-in tracer addition prior to processing.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation processed through each envelope to confirm capture/protection assay performance. Negative controls: buffer-only runs, detergent-disrupted aliquots, and capture-reagent compatibility panels for buffers used in TFF/depth filter runs.
dependencies: Availability of >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank/passage range
Access to TFF hardware supporting programmable TMP/flux and cassette rotation
Validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation and spike-in tracer availability
Analytical capacity for density-fractionation and protection assays
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (1) no reproducible preservation of orthogonal intact-EV signatures in the staged low-shear arm across lots (falsified hypothesis), or (2) spike-in tracer fails to show consistent recovery/membrane-protection (assay failure requiring redesign).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If the failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified: staged low-shear concentration does not prevent scale-dependent loss of intact-EV signature. The program should deprioritize TFF-envelope modification as the dominant mitigator and investigate alternative drivers (upstream source-cell variability, fractionation strategy, formulation/device compatibility) or accept secretome-centric approaches.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A staged low-shear TFF concentration envelope preserves intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks; detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) across independent lots at scale-proxy conditions, while high-flux TFF parameters produce reproducible loss of that signature despite similar bulk particle counts.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation of co-localization between particle-count peaks and capture-positive fractions in the staged low-shear arm and clear loss of that co-localization in the high-flux comparator across >=3 independent lots; captured signal must be substantially reduced after detergent + protease/RNase in preserved samples (indicative of membrane protection). Spike-in tracer must be recovered and show membrane-protection behavior to validate assay performance.
experiment.question: Does a staged low-shear concentration envelope (reduced TMP/flux per cassette + cassette rotation + inline gentle depth prefilter) preserve an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature and provide qualitatively acceptable recovery compared with the program's current high-flux TFF envelope when run at scale-proxy cumulative processed volumes?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) large enough to perform matched scale-proxy TFF runs (>=3 independent biological lots recommended)
TFF system capable of controlled TMP/flux and cassette rotation; membranes representative of manufacturing cassettes
Inline gentle depth prefilter cartridges for test arm
Standard TFF hardware/configuration representing current high-flux envelope (comparator arm)
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents) and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to control recovery
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent)
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio differences post-concentration between arms
Recovered particle and mass yield (qualitative assessment for manufacturability) per arm
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
Capture-compatibility control results to exclude assay interference
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the staged low-shear envelope reproducibly shows (A) particle-count peak(s) that co-localize with capture-positive signal in density/size fractions, (B) captured signal that is substantially reduced after detergent + protease/RNase treatment (membrane protection), and (C) recovered particle/mass yield judged qualitatively sufficient for preliminary GMP-like batch considerations. The high-flux comparator shows reproducible loss of the orthogonal intact-EV signature under matched conditions while maintaining similar bulk particle counts.

explicit_inferences: If low-shear staged concentration preserves orthogonal intact-EV signatures across independent lots while high-flux TFF conditions do not, then a scale-control acceptance gate can be defined around the low-shear envelope to reduce manufacturing risk.
falsification_criteria: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots processed under matched scale-proxy conditions, if the staged low-shear TFF envelope does not reproducibly preserve capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks or captured signal remains detergent/protease-insensitive (i.e., signature lost) compared with high-flux TFF, the hypothesis is falsified.
If spike-in tracer controls indicate assay failure (inconsistent recovery), interpretation is invalid and experiment must be redesigned.
human_decisions_required: Approve use of staged low-shear envelope for pilot-scale runs and provide acceptable qualitative yield thresholds for decision
Approve selection of exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (species/label) and capture-panel reagents
manufacturability_assessment: The staged low-shear envelope is implementable using existing TFF hardware with parameter control (TMP/flux limits, cassette rotation schedule) and addition of commercially available depth prefilters. Yield risk exists if overly conservative TMP/flux limits reduce recovery; pilot-scale runs will be required to confirm qualitative manufacturability prior to GMP-like batches.
manufacturing_rationale: If a low-shear staged concentration envelope preserves orthogonal intact-EV identity signals while yielding materially sufficient particle/mass recovery, it defines an operational TFF envelope usable as a manufacturing control to separate analytic noise from true scale effects and to allow downstream comparability/potency development without wholesale process redesign.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow applied to post-concentration outputs: (1) density-gradient or SEC fractionation with particle counting per fraction (NTA/TRPS), (2) immuno-capture of canonical EV surface markers on intact material per fraction (ELISA/bead-capture), (3) protease and RNase protection assays with and without detergent to assess membrane protection, (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction, and (5) spike-in intact-EV tracer recovery to control assay performance and rule out capture-reagent incompatibility.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis proposes a genuinely new, operational manufacturing intervention — a staged low-shear concentration envelope combining reduced per-cassette TMP/flux, cassette rotation, and an inline gentle depth prefilter — explicitly designed to isolate and prevent a scale-dependent intact-EV signature loss mechanism. Prior program hypotheses explored whether TFF parameters correlate with signature loss; this proposal tests a different, actionable engineering mitigation (a modified processing envelope) and includes spike-in assay controls and yield evaluation to discriminate assay artifacts from true TFF-driven damage.
principal_risks: Staged low-shear envelope may reduce recovery yields below manufacturable thresholds.
Assay interference could confound interpretation; spike-in controls and buffer-compatibility panels are required.
Even with preserved identity, cross-species delivery barriers may still prevent in vivo exposure.
proposed_potency_relationship: This hypothesis addresses identity/stability risk rather than potency directly. If identity is preserved through the scale-control, it enables later potency linking experiments but does not assert potency itself.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a scale-control operating envelope: staged low-shear TFF concentration (defined TMP/flux limits per cassette, cassette-rotation schedule, and an inline gentle depth prefilter) that demonstrably preserves an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature and provides acceptable qualitative yield for downstream bounded small-EV drug-substance definition.
title: Hypothesis: A low-shear, cassette-sequenced concentration strategy (modified TFF + inline depth prefilter) prevents scale-dependent loss of intact-EV analytical signature observed with standard high-flux TFF
